payload.rebuttal: fixed: Same fix as #1 — the two findings point at the same defect (restore_mutant's reliance on content.count(mutant.replace.encode()) == 1) from two angles. The rewritten restore_mutant no longer performs that count at all, so an empty replace is no longer special-cased or rejected; it round-trips like any other mutant because the recorded offset, not a search, is what restore now uses.
